question.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
question.text: The defeated Ishida said that he fought for the heir of this man. Known by the nicknames of "the monkey" and "the bald rat" because of his looks, his actions included the reunification of Japan and the invasion of Japan.
question.clue: Forces under this man lost the Battle of (+) Hansan Island due to the "crane formation" during one invasion, and that invasion later ended after this man's forces were defeated at Noryang by Yi Sun-sin.

swap.leadin: Following the failure of the Shimabara Rebellion during this period, Christians were forced underground.
swap.text: Name this last shogunate [show-gun-ate] of Japan. Commodore Matthew Perry entered Japan while this shogunate was in power.
swap.clue: Because of the Shimbara rebellion, this period's government increased its proscription of Christians.

question.leadin: Saigo Takamori was an influential member of this class.
question.text: Name this class of warrior nobility from feudal Japan. Members of this class traditionally carried both a long katana and a shorter sword.
question.clue: Members of this group could find a job by embarking on a type of pilgrimage called musha shugyo, and their only goal should be "to grasp the long and the short swords and to die".

swap.leadin: Holders of this title, which originated in the Heian (hay-ahn) period, ruled from the Bakufu.
swap.text: Holding power until the 1867 Meiji (may-jee) Restoration, name this title that denoted military rulers of Japan such as Ashikaga Takauji.
swap.clue: After the arrival of the "black ships," the isolationist rule of this office was ended with the Convention of Kanagawa, shortly before they were made obsolete with the Meiji Restoration.

question.leadin: Rudolf von Gneist helped create a new constitution during this period.
question.text: Name this period in Japanese history following the end of the Tokugawa Shogunate. This period is named for an emperor whose reign saw a resurgence of imperial power.
question.clue: Its goals were delineated in the Charter Oath, which expressed the desire break away from the "evil customs of the past."

swap.text: Irezumi and ohaguro both flourished in popularity during this period of Japanese history. This period, which is typically seen as a period of prosperity and artistic development, was ended by the Meiji Restoration.
swap.clue: Its end is known by a term meaning "closing of the curtain."

question.leadin: This political leader reigned supreme over local lords known as daimyo, and the last ones were descendants and relatives of Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.text: Name this warlord who had real power in Japan prior to the Meiji restoration.
question.clue: Two successive dynasties in this position supported the illegitimate Northern Court.

swap.text: Although the shogunate was centered on Kamakura, the official capital and residence of the emperor remained this western city, whose name simply means "capital city."
swap.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

question.text: This first shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was dominated by the Hojo family.
question.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Tokugawa shogunate.
swap.text: In 1638, the Tokugawa government put down this rebellion of Japanese Christians by storming Hara Castle and beheading its leader, Shiro.
swap.clue: The Tokugawa Shogunate put down this 1630s rebellion of Japanese Catholics that led to the expulsion of Portuguese traders.

question.leadin: It ended as the Minamoto clan prevailed over the Taira clan in the Gempei Wars.
question.text: Name this pre-shogun period of Japanese history. At this point in time, the Imperial officials were mere puppets to the Fujiwara nobility, classical Japanese literature flourished, and the capital was in modern-day Kyoto.
question.clue: Starting in this period, proprietors called ryoke would hand money to government inspectors to preserve the tax-free status of their sh¯oen estates.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about a nation's history.
swap.text: During the Muromachi period this clan held the shogunate. Members included Takauji and Yoshimitsu.
swap.clue: A ruler of this family promoted the "Higashiyama culture" of the eastern hills, which popularized shoin ("sho-een") homes with tatami floors; his aesthetic was exemplified by the "wabi-sabi" style of a temple that he couldn't afford to coat in silver.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about famous war photographers.
question.text: Joe Rosenthal took an iconic image of five marines raising a flag on this Pacific Island during World War II. Clint Eastwood directed a film told from the Japanese perspective called Letters from This place.
question.clue: The February to March 1945 struggle for this island at Meatgrinder Hill and Mount Suribachi ended with a certain flag-raising.

swap.text: This research group under the Kwantung Army committed some of the greatest Japanese crimes against humanity during the war. It was commanded by Shiro Ishii, who was pardoned by the United States after the war in exchange for his data.
swap.answerHtml: Unit 731 [accept Nana-san-ichi Butai; accept Epidemic Prevention and Water Purification Department of the Kwantung Army; accept Kantogun Boeki Kyusuibu Honbu]
swap.clue: This group within the Epidemic Prevention and Purification Department. A guy actually named Colonel Sanders brought it to the attention of Douglas MacArthur, who pardoned its leader in exchange for scientific data.

question.text: High-fired grey pottery called Sue was introduced by the Gaya Confederacy to Japan during this era of Japanese history, named for its keyhole-shaped tombs.
question.clue: This part of the Yamato period which transitioned to the Asuka period with the introduction of Buddhism to Japan. This Japanese era was named after large keyhole-shaped tombs.

swap.text: The Toyotomi clan was overthrown by this man, who expelled all Christians from Japan in 1614. The shogunate set up by this man ruled Japan until the Meiji Restoration.
swap.clue: As head of the Eastern Army, this man defeated the forces of Ishida Mitsunari at the Battle of Sekigahara.

question.text: Rusk told Yang that the maritime Macarthur Line would hold until this 1951 treaty took effect. This treaty names the US's "system" of "hub and spokes" bilateral defense treaties with Pacific countries, especially Japan.
question.answerHtml: Treaty of San Francisco [or San Furanshisuko kōwa-Jōyaku; prompt on Treaty of Peace with Japan or U.S.-Japan Security Treaty (or Japanese equivalents) with “In what city was that treaty signed?]

swap.text: Because the red dye beni was forbidden for commoners to use, kimonos were dyed red using pigments bought on this island, where a trading post was built in 1639 after one on nearby Hirado Island burned down.
swap.clue: One country's first female doctor was born to botanist Philipp Franz von Siebold after he met a woman in this place, though he was expelled after acquiring illegal maps.

question.leadin: You are a Tokugawa official tasked with uncovering Kakure Kirishitan, or hidden Christians. You also have a terrible secret of your own: you are Auroni Gupta.
question.text: You hope no one notices your UCSD sweatshirt under your kimono as you try to identify Kirishitan by seeing who refuses to step on these flat images of Christian symbols, whose name literally means "stepping- on pictures."
question.clue: Under the Tokugawa shogunate, Nagasaki Christians were often required to step on these depictions of Jesus or the Virgin Mary, at the risk of torture. These objects were usually made from bronze or painted stone.

swap.text: In the 1651 Keian Uprising, Yui Shosetsu gathered an army of these master-less mercenary samurai and attempted to overthrow the Tokugawa Shogunate.
swap.clue: In modern Japan, salarymen are often referred to as these people if they are unemployed.
